newsitem.title: GERMANY: Easter break complicates German call money trading.
newsitem.headline: Easter break complicates German call money trading.

text.p: German call money was trading slightly higher on Monday, with the market already starting to look ahead to a difficult month-end, complicated by the Easter holiday break.
Dealers said call money was trading at 3.08/12 percent, with the majority of trades taking place at 3.10 percent. This was slightly higher than Friday's morning price o 3.05/10.

Dealers said the market was not particularly well-endowed with funds but added that it was very difficult to assess reserve levels and requirements due to the long holiday period. Markets will be closed for Easter on Friday and Monday.
The Bundesbank said today that the estimated reserve requirement for March will be 39.5 billion marks.
Banks held 40.8 billion marks of funds in reserve accounts at the central bank on Friday, giving an average of 40.8 billion for the month to Sunday, March 23.
Dealers were waiting to see how much the Bundesbank allocated to the market in this week's repo tender, which will offset an expiring 80.1 billion mark pact.
The extent to which this would be fully offset was seen dependent on market developments over the next two days.
Banks took up only a negligible amount of funding at the 4.50 percent Lombard emergency funding rate on Friday.
The Frankfurt Interbank Overnight Average FIONA= was calculated at 3.14433 on Monday compared with 3.12400 on Friday.
